decided: A sensor reads the plan it compares against, and its own settings, as they stood just before the commit that records the start of building, and reads both from the saved history rather than from the files as they are now. It measures every change committed for this work since the work's first saved commit, so code saved together with the plan is measured too. Before building has started, it compares against the plan as it stands. When there is no saved history, or nothing of the work is saved yet, it reports that it cannot read, never that it found nothing.
alternatives: Take the first saved commit that touches anything outside the work's own folders as the start of building, and measure from there.
Take the commit that records the start of building, and measure only from there.
Read the plan and the settings from the files as they are now.
why: Measured over the 14 latest finished changes, the first rule mistook a review fix of the architecture doc for the start of building three times, and it never measured code saved together with the plan; measuring only from the start of building misses that code too; and files as they are now can be changed by the run being watched without leaving any saved trace.

defines.definition: The project's record of every committed version of its files, kept by git.

detail: Fixed point = parent of the earliest first-parent commit adding orbit/changes/<name>/.orbit-runs/apply-*.json; measure = git diff --numstat --no-renames -z <first commit>^..HEAD; before the apply emit is committed the reference is HEAD (frozen: false); no-git and uncommitted are cannot-read reasons (design M1, M2; the proposal walk's option B for F1, ratified by the user).
